The feeder identifier pinpoints a specific electrical distribution segment serving a limited geographic area (70 housing units in this case). Combined with other columns, it enables re-identification of specific households or businesses within that area. Under data minimization and purpose limitation principles, this level of geographic granularity should be generalized or pseudonymized.

The substation identifier, combined with the feeder, narrows the geographic scope to a very specific area. This constitutes a quasi-identifier that, in combination with consumption data, could facilitate re-identification of individual consumers. Data protection principles require that such locational identifiers be pseudonymized or generalized.

While the date provides temporal specificity, it is a standard analytical dimension in energy data and does not directly identify individuals. On its own, it carries low re-identification risk. However, when combined with feeder/substation and consumption patterns, it increases the granularity of the data point. General date-level data is typically retained for analytical purposes.
